text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV-2 - elevated errors on streaming / function-calling paths. Pager: @Anna. Start: 2026-03-15T09:01:08Z. Symptoms: SSE disconnects, tool-call JSON parse errors. Affected route: /v1/streaming/generate (hosted). Notifying on-call and SRE ops.

Anna: Taking this. Thanks. What do we know about customer impact so far?

John: Support seeing multiple tickets: 3 tenants reporting sudden failures around 09:00-09:10 UTC. Error in client logs: `JSON error: unexpected end of input` and some `SSE connection closed` logs. Screenshots attached in tickets.

Dheeraj: On it. Can someone paste runtime logs/traces or correlation ids? I'll start with ingress metrics.

Maria: Pasting quick trace snippets from runtime (truncated):
```
2026-03-15T09:02:11Z runtime-01 ERROR toolcall_parser: parse_error: unexpected end of input, id=abc123, bytes_received=104
2026-03-15T09:02:11Z runtime-01 WARN sse: client_disconnect: remote=10.12.5.9 conn=fd234
2026-03-15T09:02:12Z runtime-02 INFO handler: handoff_to_fallback id=abc123 route=/v1/streaming/generate
```
These lines repeat intermittently across hosts. Looks like payloads arriving incomplete then parser throws.

Kevin: We didn't deploy anything to hosted runtime in the last 48h. But a small change shipped to the SDK (okhttp bump) might have rolled out to some clients yesterday. Could be client-side chunking / boundary change + our parser expecting complete tool-call frames.

Dheeraj: Observed spike in concurrent streaming connections at ~08:58 UTC. Also increase in `read timeout` errors in proxy logs.

Maria: Another log excerpt from proxy: 
```
proxy-03 2026-03-15T09:01:58Z WARN stream: read_timeout remote=client-a user-agent="okhttp/4.9.3"
proxy-03 2026-03-15T09:01:58Z INFO stream: upstream_close code=200 bytes=0
```
Suggests clients dropped connection mid-stream.

Kevin: Hypothesis list (ranked):
- H1: Client library behavior changed (chunking/keepalive) + our parser assumes frame-delimited JSON -> truncated frames -> parse errors.
- H2: Ingress proxy transiently failing under concurrency -> partial payloads delivered.
- H3: Runtime edge case where KV cache flush interacts with streaming serialization -> truncated payloads (lower pri).

Anna: From support: customer impact summary so far: 3 tenants, one enterprise Dedicated, ~12k streaming requests touched, error rate spike ~2.3% for streaming calls during window. Customers report degraded feature (toolcall failures), no data loss beyond retries.

Carla: Noted for product: one customer is on a critical flow. They saw production errors for ~10 minutes. Support ticket IDs: #4567, #4569, #4571. We should prepare comms if this escalates.

Dheeraj: Immediate mitigations I'm applying now:
- Route affected tenant IDs to non-streaming polling fallback (admin routing change) for mitigation (5% -> 100% if bad).
- Increase proxy read timeout from 30s -> 60s on canary hosts.
- Deploy permissive parser fallback that buffers until end-of-stream for tool-call frames (hotfix) as a try-catch.

Maria: I pushed the routing canary (5% traffic) at 09:06 UTC and increased read timeout on two canary proxies. Monitoring dashboards updated.

Kevin: Guidance for SDK teams: ask clients to upgrade to latest SDK which includes retry-on-incomplete-chunk behavior. Also add doc note about streaming boundaries.

John: Support: notified affected customers about mitigation (routing fallback) and asked for SDK versions. Two customers reported `okhttp/4.9.3` in their logs.

Dheeraj: Quick correlation query I ran (ingress): `select count(*) from requests where route='/v1/streaming/generate' and status!='200' and ts between '2026-03-15T08:55' and '2026-03-15T09:15' group by tenant` -> shows spikes aligned to tickets.

Maria: Added raw parser stack trace to the incident thread (copied below):
```
runtime: toolcall_parser.go:215: decodeFrame -> json.Unmarshal -> EOF -> return parse_error
stack: toolcall_parser.decodeFrame -> handler.processStream -> runtime.serveStream
```
This is consistent with partial payloads.

Kevin: Quick test against a local client simulating chunked frames (okhttp 4.9.3) produced same `EOF` in parser if the client closed connection mid-chunk. That strongly supports H1.

Dheeraj: Live mitigation status: routing canary at 5% -> reduced error rate for those tenants to ~0.4%. Increasing to 20% now. If stable, will flip 100% for affected tenants.

Anna: Customer impact assessment updated: currently contained, mitigation applied. Oncall notes: followup RCA needed to decide long-term fix (parser hardened vs stricter contract with SDKs).

Carla: Please add priority to enterprise customer, coordinate proactive comms if we flip 100% and it persists.

Kevin: Long-term action items (to track in postmortem):
- Harden streaming parser to handle partial/mid-chunk reconnect semantics + robust reassembly.
- Add automated regression test with multiple client SDK versions and chunking patterns.
- Add monitoring alert for `parse_error: EOF` spikes.
- Update SDK compatibility matrix and docs.

Dheeraj: I'm creating postmortem issue and will assign to @Dheeraj, @Maria, @Kevin. Tagging support and product for comms.

Anna: Good. Please include timeline snippets (we have the logs). I'll sign off on incident once routing flip completes and error rates return to baseline.

Maria: Routing flip to 100% for affected tenants completed at 09:18 UTC. Error rate returned to baseline by 09:23 UTC.

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged as mitigated by Anna at 2026-03-15T09:25:00Z. Please file RCA and link it here. :white_check_mark:

Anna: Thanks all. Postmortem owner: Dheeraj. Action owners will be in the ticket. Closing live thread, moving to postmortem channel once draft is ready.

Kevin: Quick note for follow-up: add an integration test in CI that simulates okhttp chunk boundaries.

John: Support will follow up with customers and close tickets after validation.

Carla: Adding stakeholder update in product channel.

Dheeraj: I'll drop final timeline + log snippets into the postmortem doc.

Anna: Thread closed for live mitigation. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
